settings.html: Why it matters in Iowa

settings.title: Why Fall Heating Maintenance Matters in Iowa

settings.editor: Iowa winters don't ease into it—one week it's mild, the next it's sub-zero for ten days straight. Your furnace goes from resting all summer to running almost nonstop. A tune-up before that shift does four things that actually matter:
The #1 reason to service a gas furnace is safety. We inspect the heat exchanger for cracks and test for carbon monoxide—an invisible, odorless gas that a neglected furnace can leak into your home.
A dirty burner, clogged filter, or failing part forces your system to burn more fuel for the same heat. A tuned furnace runs at peak efficiency, and that shows up on every winter bill.
Most no-heat emergencies trace back to a worn part we could have spotted and replaced during a calm fall visit—instead of at 2 a.m. in January.
Most manufacturers require documented annual maintenance to keep your equipment warranty valid. Skip it, and a future repair could come out of your own pocket.

settings.html: What's included

settings.title: What's Included in a Lenz Heating Tune-Up

settings.editor: This isn't a quick look-and-go. Our technicians run your system through a full inspection, cleaning, and safety test so nothing gets missed.

settings.html:
• Inspect heat exchanger for cracks or corrosion
  • Test for carbon monoxide leaks
  • Check and clean burners and flame sensor
  • Test ignition and safety controls
  • Measure gas pressure and connections
  • Inspect flue and venting
  • Check and calibrate thermostat
  • Inspect blower motor and amp draw
  • Test full startup and shutdown cycle
  • Replace or inspect air filter

• Check refrigerant charge and lines
  • Test the reversing valve and defrost cycle
  • Inspect and clean coils
  • Verify auxiliary/backup heat operation
  • Test electrical connections and contactors
  • Inspect and calibrate thermostat
  • Check airflow and inspect the air filter
  • Test the full heating cycle
Know the signs

settings.title: Signs Your Heating System Is Overdue for Service

settings.editor: You don't always have to wait for a breakdown. Schedule a tune-up sooner if you notice any of these:

settings.html:
• Higher heating bills than last winter with no change in usage
  • Uneven heat—some rooms warm, others always cold
  • Strange smells when the heat kicks on (a burning or musty odor)
  • Odd noises—banging, rattling, squealing, or clicking
  • Short cycling—the system turns on and off rapidly
  • Weak airflow from your vents
  • It's been over a year since your last professional service

settings.editor: Choosing who works on your heating system isn't just about the wrench—it's about who you trust in your home when it's cold out and something's wrong.
No hidden fees, no surprise hourly charges. The quote we give you before we start is the exact number on your final bill.

settings.html: FAQs

Once a year, ideally in the fall before heating season begins. If you have a heat pump that both heats and cools, we recommend twice-yearly service—once before winter and once before summer.

Early fall, before the first cold snap. Booking in September or October gets your system ready ahead of the rush and well before you actually need the heat.

Yes. A tune-up typically pays for itself through lower energy bills, fewer breakdowns, and a longer equipment lifespan—and it keeps your manufacturer warranty valid, which can save you far more on a future repair.

Maintenance is proactive—inspecting, cleaning, and tuning a working system to prevent problems. Repair fixes something that's already broken. Regular maintenance is what helps you avoid the repair in the first place.
